links.outcome: Clinician signoff with no or minor edits, LLM vs clinician-written discharge summaries on same admissions
links.effect: LLM minus clinician signoff difference 22.2 percentage points (95% CI, 19.0-27.5); lower bound exceeded the -5 point noninferiority margin, demonstrating noninferiority.
links.quote: The absolute difference in model-estimated probability of signoff with no or minor edits (LLM generated minus clinician authored) was 22.2 percentage points (95% CI, 19.0-27.5 percentage points); the lower bound exceeded the prespecified noninferiority margin of -5 percentage points, demonstrating noninferiority.

links.outcome: Independent physician review of AI-generated summaries against the full record for accuracy and potential harm
links.effect: 12 physicians rated LLM summaries higher on accuracy, completeness, tone, clarity (risk differences 19.4 to 29.1 points); harm rating ≥3 in 26.2% and 26.8% vs 45.1% and 51.5% for clinician-authored.
links.quote: LLM-generated summaries also had a lower proportion of cases rated 3 or greater for potential harm on the clinical summary and plan and requested actions sections (140 of 534 [26.2%] and 124 of 462 [26.8%]) compared with clinician-authored summaries (271 of 601 [45.1%] and 278 of 540 [51.5%]).

screen.reason: Retrospective comparative evaluation of clinician acceptance and ratings of LLM-generated vs clinician-authored discharge summaries without testing a specific deployment safeguard or practice comparison.
